citation: Dahy 2025, Tracing the Heat: LULC changes and urban heat island dynamics in Abu Dhabi

citation: Hamdan 2021, Physicochemical characterization and seasonal variations of PM10 aerosols in a harsh environment

citation: Hamdan 2021, Physicochemical characterization and seasonal variations of PM10 aerosols in a harsh environment

citation: EAD 2018, Abu Dhabi Air Emissions Inventory

citation: Teixido 2021, The influence of COVID-19 preventive measures on the air quality in Abu Dhabi

citation: Pfannerstill 2019, Shipborne measurements of total OH reactivity around the Arabian Peninsula and its role in ozone chemistry

citation: Pfannerstill 2019, Shipborne measurements of total OH reactivity around the Arabian Peninsula and its role in ozone chemistry

citation: Matthaios 2022, Quantifying factors affecting contributions of roadway exhaust and non-exhaust emissions to ambient PM10-2.5 and PM2.5-0.2

citation: Matthaios 2022, Quantifying factors affecting contributions of roadway exhaust and non-exhaust emissions to ambient PM10-2.5 and PM2.5-0.2

citation: Matthaios 2022, Quantifying factors affecting contributions of roadway exhaust and non-exhaust emissions to ambient PM10-2.5 and PM2.5-0.2
evidence: Relative humidity together with wind speed was significantly associated with coarse and fine road dust resuspension, combined relative importance 38 % and 48 %, higher humidity suppressing resuspension.

citation: Alahmad 2024, Combined impact of heat and dust on diabetes hospitalization in Kuwait

citation: Alahmad 2024, Combined impact of heat and dust on diabetes hospitalization in Kuwait

citation: Alahmad 2024, Combined impact of heat and dust on diabetes hospitalization in Kuwait
evidence: Compared with mild non-dusty days at 33 degC and 0 ug/m3, hot-dusty days raised the relative risk of unplanned diabetic admissions from 1.11 at 42 degC and 85 ug/m3 to 1.36 at 42 degC and 150 ug/m3.

citation: Alahmad 2024, Combined impact of heat and dust on diabetes hospitalization in Kuwait
evidence: Each year 282 excess diabetic admissions were attributed to hot days and about 114 excess admissions per 10 ug/m3 of dust, with combined hot-dusty conditions exacerbating the hospitalization risk further.

citation: Dons 2019, Transport most likely to cause air pollution peak exposures in everyday life

citation: Jeong 2018, Characteristics of peak concentrations of black carbon encountered by elementary school children

citation: Jeong 2018, Characteristics of peak concentrations of black carbon encountered by elementary school children
evidence: Trips by diesel vehicle produced frequent long-duration peaks above the 95th percentile, walking produced brief high peaks from passing or idling vehicles, and peaks during commuting showed relatively high exposure intensity on weekdays.

citation: Jeong 2018, Characteristics of peak concentrations of black carbon encountered by elementary school children
evidence: Cooking led to frequent peak occurrences, charbroiling meat incurred sustained peaks as intense as trips by diesel vehicles, and cooking peaks accounted for an elevated residential contribution to daily integrated exposure.

citation: Tong 2025, Further improvement in London's air quality demands more than the ULEZ

citation: Jezek Brecelj 2025, On-road vehicle emissions measurements show a significant reduction in black carbon and NOx in Euro 6c and 6d diesel cars

citation: GSO 2025, Implementation guideline for new vehicle emission limits in the UAE

citation: GSO 2025, Implementation guideline for new vehicle emission limits in the UAE

citation: Adar 2015, Adopting clean fuels and technologies on school buses: pollution and health impacts in children
evidence: Fine and ultrafine particle concentrations measured on 597 trips on 188 school buses were 10 to 50 % lower on buses using ultralow-sulfur diesel, diesel oxidation catalysts and/or closed crankcase ventilation.

citation: Adar 2015, Adopting clean fuels and technologies on school buses: pollution and health impacts in children
evidence: Ultrafine particle concentrations on buses were 10 to 50 % lower with ULSD, DOCs and/or CCVs adopted between 2005 and 2009.

citation: Adar 2015, Adopting clean fuels and technologies on school buses: pollution and health impacts in children
evidence: ULSD adoption was associated with 8 % lower absenteeism (95 % CI -16.0 to -0.7 %) among 275 bus riders, and extrapolated to the US population changed fuels and technologies likely reduced absenteeism by more than 14 million days per year.

citation: Adar 2015, Adopting clean fuels and technologies on school buses: pollution and health impacts in children
evidence: ULSD adoption was associated with greater changes in FVC and FEV1 of 0.02 and 0.01 L per year and reduced exhaled nitric oxide by 16 %, with DOCs and CCVs also associated with improved FVC growth.

citation: Adar 2015, Adopting clean fuels and technologies on school buses: pollution and health impacts in children
evidence: Reduced FeNO, improved lung function and lower absenteeism after clean bus technology showed stronger associations among patients with asthma, and DOC and CCV benefits were primarily restricted to children with persistent asthma.

citation: Bursey 2025, Health, economic, and environmental impacts of electric school bus adoption: a scoping review

citation: Bursey 2025, Health, economic, and environmental impacts of electric school bus adoption: a scoping review
evidence: Children riding diesel school buses are exposed to diesel pollutants, and electrification efforts in high-income countries rely on external funding programmes, so the bus fleet that is provided determines the technology standard it can be held to.

citation: Orellano 2024, Long-term exposure to particulate matter and mortality: an update of the WHO global air quality guidelines systematic review and meta-analysis

citation: Chen 2020, Long-term exposure to PM and all-cause and cause-specific mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis

citation: Hamra 2015, Lung cancer and exposure to nitrogen dioxide and traffic: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence: The meta-estimate across 20 studies for the change in lung cancer associated with a 10 ug/m3 increase in NO2 was 4 % (95 % CI 1 to 8 %), and 3 % (1 to 5 %) per 10 ug/m3 NOx.

citation: Hamra 2015, Lung cancer and exposure to nitrogen dioxide and traffic: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence: Forest plots for measures of traffic volume and distance to roadways largely suggest a modest increase in lung cancer risk, and residential proximity to roadways suggests increased risk attributable partly to air pollution exposure.

citation: Boogaard 2022, Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution and selected health outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence: The HEI panel review of 353 studies found high or moderate-to-high confidence in an association between long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution and lung cancer mortality.

citation: Boogaard 2022, Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution and selected health outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence: The HEI panel found high or moderate-to-high confidence in an association between long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution and asthma onset in adults, alongside asthma onset in children.

citation: Liu 2021, Long-term exposure to low-level air pollution and incidence of asthma: the ELAPSE project
evidence: Among 98,326 adults in Denmark and Sweden with 1,965 incident asthma cases, the hazard ratio was 1.17 (95 % CI 1.10 to 1.25) per 10 ug/m3 NO2, unchanged in two-pollutant models with PM2.5, with no evidence of a threshold.

citation: Liu 2021, Long-term exposure to low-level air pollution and incidence of asthma: the ELAPSE project
evidence: Adult asthma incidence hazard ratio was 1.15 (95 % CI 1.08 to 1.23) per 0.5 x 10-5 m-1 black carbon, and the BC estimate remained unchanged in two-pollutant models with PM2.5.

citation: Liu 2021, Long-term exposure to low-level air pollution and incidence of asthma: the ELAPSE project

citation: Jacquemin 2015, Ambient air pollution and adult asthma incidence in six European cohorts (ESCAPE)

citation: Bourtsoukidis 2019, Non-methane hydrocarbon (C2 to C8) sources and sinks around the Arabian Peninsula
evidence: C2 to C8 hydrocarbons reached several ppb over the Arabian Gulf with a maximum of 166.5 ppb of alkanes, and an i-pentane to n-pentane ratio of 0.93 over the Gulf is indicative of widespread oil and gas activities.

citation: Bourtsoukidis 2019, Non-methane hydrocarbon (C2 to C8) sources and sinks around the Arabian Peninsula
evidence: International shipping contributes to ambient C3 to C8 hydrocarbon concentrations but not to ethane, and the i-pentane to n-pentane ratio of 1.71 in the Suez Canal is a characteristic signature of ship emissions.

citation: Pfannerstill 2019, Shipborne measurements of total OH reactivity around the Arabian Peninsula and its role in ozone chemistry

citation: Jo 2001, Exposure to methyl tertiary butyl ether and benzene in close proximity to service stations
evidence: Residents in neighbourhoods near service stations are exposed to elevated ambient MTBE and benzene levels (outdoor benzene mean 1.7 ppb) compared with those living farther away, and service stations were the major contributor to residents' MTBE exposure.

citation: Jeong 2025, Spatial variation of resuspended particulate matter in urban environments and real-world assessment of street sweeping

citation: Jeong 2025, Spatial variation of resuspended particulate matter in urban environments and real-world assessment of street sweeping
evidence: Because resuspended PM was highest on local streets, school neighbourhoods in residential areas and open spaces may experience acute exposure to road dust PM.

citation: Amato 2010, A review on the effectiveness of street sweeping, washing and dust suppressants as urban PM control methods
evidence: Road dust emissions from paved roads arise from particles already deposited and easily resuspended by traffic-generated turbulence, carrying heavy metals from vehicle wear particles and coarse PM2.5-10, and sweeping, water flushing and chemical suppressants are the measures used against them.
